name: Summer and Academic Year Youth Internships (Museum of Science)
grades: Enrolled in high school or an equivalent program
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the museum pages.
duration: The summer program is 7 weeks. The academic year program runs during the school year. Hours are not stated.
deadline_text: No openings were posted when checked on Oct 9, 2026. The museum says summer internships are usually recruited in February or March and fall ones in June or July, but timing can change. Deadlines are listed in each posting.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19. You must be in high school or an equivalent program.
how_to_apply: Watch the museum's internship job board. Use View Internships on the Museum of Science internships page. Apply to the youth internship posting when it opens.
notes: The museum pages do not say if the internships are paid, so ask before you apply. Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) says a child needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools to be employed. The museum also has Youth Volunteers, ages 14 to 19 and in high school. The volunteer page gives no application steps beyond a general interest form. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Summer Teen Internship Program
pay_detail: All teen internships are paid positions (rate not stated)
duration: One week of training and six weeks of work
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back next March for the summer 2027 application.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. Most internships are open to residents of Boston and Cambridge.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens (expected next March). Interns also attend a weekly professional development course and an ocean advocacy course. Questions: teens@neaq.org.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (the aquarium page does not mention it; M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the state Attorney General's Office, cover the permit rule). The aquarium also runs ClimaTeens (ages 13 and up, 2026-27 applications due October 18, 2026).

name: Accelerate Pre-College Programs, Boston campus (Northeastern)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $6,995 and includes tuition, course materials, housing, meals and social activities. Need based financial aid is available, and a non-refundable deposit of 20 percent of tuition (after aid and discounts) holds your spot. Priority round applicants get a $500 discount.
duration: Twelve days, move in on Sunday and move out the following Friday. Summer 2027 session dates were not posted on the pages read.
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2027 applications open in early December. Priority deadline January 15, regular February 28 and late March 15, each at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The page does not print the year with these three dates. Deposit deadlines are February 18 (priority), April 1 (regular) and April 15 (late), and full tuition is due May 1.
who_can_apply: High school rising juniors and seniors from the US and around the world. (The 17 or older rule on the page applies only to the London program.)
how_to_apply: Send in the online application. Add an unofficial high school transcript or report card. Add a personal statement of up to 250 words. A teacher or counselor reference is optional. You ask for financial aid inside the application.
notes: Expensive. The program page says the Summer 2027 offerings were still being finalized and will be posted later this fall. For a free Northeastern option for Massachusetts juniors see the Young Scholars Program card.

name: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
grades: Entering 12th grade in the fall (current juniors)
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend is mentioned on the page.
duration: About six weeks. 2027 dates: June 22 to July 31, 2027, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., in person on the Northeastern campus.
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 14, 2026 and close March 1, 2027 at 5 p.m. Teacher recommendations are due March 8 or 9 (the page lists both dates).
who_can_apply: Current juniors. You must be a permanent Massachusetts resident. That means you live and go to school in MA all year. You must live within commuting distance of campus. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Online Student Application. It takes 60 to 90 minutes. You cannot save it or restart it. So write the essay answers ahead of time. You also need two teacher recommendations. A STEM teacher is best. Enter the recommenders' email addresses in the application.
notes: Free, but only for Massachusetts residents who are US citizens or permanent residents. Late applications are not accepted. Read the program FAQ before emailing the coordinator. The same page also has a line saying applications are due March 2nd, 2026, which conflicts with the March 1, 2027 close date. Confirm the 2027 date with the program before you plan around it.

name: Youth Conservation Corps, National Parks of Boston
org: National Park Service, Boston National Historical Park
pay_detail: $16.00 per hour
duration: 2026 schedule: Monday June 29 to Friday August 21, about 30 to 35 hours a week, 9 AM to 4 PM
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed April 26, 2026 at 11:59 PM (rolling until then). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Must be 15 on or before the first day and not turn 19 during the program. U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident. You must live locally. You should enjoy working with kids who are 7 to 12 years old.
how_to_apply: In 2026: download the YCC application form from the park page, add 1 or 2 references, scan it and email it to npb_youthprograms@nps.gov. Applications for 2026 are closed.
notes: Paid. Mon to Fri. No housing. Work includes safety duties with young campers and training on public land management. This is a federal job, so ask the park how the Massachusetts permit rule applies. Watch the park page in early 2027. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta (club membership)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta
city: Metro Atlanta, GA (26 Clubs in 9 counties)
pay_detail: Annual membership fee. The join page lists no dollar amount. It says the fee is lower than other youth groups, is waived for youth with Amerigroup insurance, and that no child is turned away for inability to pay.
duration: Membership year (the 2026 after school registration announcement is on the home page)
deadline_text: The home page says 2026 after school registration is open. No end date read.
who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 6 to 18 may apply at each location. Each Club has its own enrollment.
how_to_apply: Use 'Register for Membership Here' on the join page, which goes to the BGCMA parent portal (bgcma.org/local-clubs/parent-portal). Use the Find a Club page to pick a Club. Headquarters phone: 404-527-7100.
notes: This is a general club membership, not a job or internship. The pages read do not describe teen specific programs or teen jobs, so call your nearest Club and ask what is offered for teens.

name: Librarians of Tomorrow
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to June 2027, 3-6 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application deadline was October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 6 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application or mail a print application to the Librarians of Tomorrow Internship Program, 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, NY 11238. Questions: LOT@bklynlibrary.org or 718-230-2406.
notes: Library teen page lists ages 15-18; the program page requires grades 10-12 in NYC. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: StoryTeen
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to May 2027, 3-5 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 5 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected applicants are contacted for an interview. Questions: storyteen@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Funded through the NYC Council's City's First Readers initiative. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teen Night Out Branch Council
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Weekly meetings Oct 2026 to June 2027, 75 hours of service
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 16-19, with a parent's signed consent for 75 hours of intern service outside school, available to meet weekly.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application. All applicants get a follow-up email and some are invited to interview.
notes: The page does not say which library branches host councils. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teaching Intern and Summer Volunteer
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.
duration: 6-week summer program
deadline_text: Not posted.
who_can_apply: The site says it recruits college and high school students as teaching interns. No age or grade rule is posted. Middle school students can also join as program students.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.

name: Canadian Cadets (Sea, Army and Air Cadets)
org: Department of National Defence (Government of Canada)
city: Local corps and squadrons across British Columbia
pay_detail: The pages read do not state a cost. The program page calls it a funded program. Ask the local unit about any fees.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register online and the unit staff contact you.
who_can_apply: Young people who are at least 12 and have not reached 19. Have your health card ready when you register.
how_to_apply: Choose Sea, Army or Air Cadets. Find a unit near you in the Corps and Squadron Directory. Register with the Online Registration Tool. Have your health card and your parents' contact details ready. Then unit staff contact you to check ID and welcome you.
notes: This is a Canada-wide program. The units in British Columbia come from the national directory. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card. A youth program, not a paid job.

name: Foundry Work & Education Program (FWEP)
pay_detail: Free. This is job and school support, not a paid job. Foundry says all its services are free and confidential.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No dates. Foundry says no referral is needed to use its services.
who_can_apply: British Columbia youth ages 15 to 24 who want to work, go to school or start a training program and face barriers to doing so. You must be legally entitled to work in BC. You should not already be working, in school or in training, or be working less than 15 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up with the online Foundry Work & Education form linked on the Foundry services page. Or find a Foundry centre near you.
notes: Foundry also gives free and confidential mental health and wellness services for youth ages 12 to 24. WorkBC also lists this program. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: SkilledTradesBC Youth Trades Programs (Discover, Explore, Train and Work in Trades)
org: SkilledTradesBC, with the Ministry of Education and Child Care
city: Across British Columbia (through your high school)
grades: High school students (grade and age rules are not stated on the pages read)
pay_detail: Youth Work in Trades training is paid, but no wage is stated. The youth programs page says tuition for these programs is covered. SkilledTradesBC and the Ministry fund technical training done in high school.
duration: From 1 high school course to a year-long program, depending on the program and trade
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the pages read. Talk to your school for dates.
who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages read give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades.

name: Skills Canada BC Competitions (regionals and provincials)
city: Regional events around British Columbia, provincials in Abbotsford
grades: Jr. Skills Projects are for grades 6 to 9. Other competitions are labelled Sec. (secondary) or PS (post-secondary).
pay_detail: No fees are listed on the pages read.
duration: Regionals in February to March 2027, provincials on April 14, 2027
deadline_text: Regionals run February to March 2027 in communities around the province, exact dates not posted yet. Provincials: April 14, 2027 at Abbotsford Tradex. Nationals: May 27 and 28, 2027 in Calgary. Registration deadlines are not listed.
who_can_apply: Students who are active at a school or college. Your teacher, instructor or career coordinator must sign you up. The exact rules are in the provincial rules document.
how_to_apply: Talk to your teacher, instructor or career coordinator. They sign you up through the Skills Canada BC registration page. It needs a password. You get it from the organization or your regional coordinator.
notes: Students cannot sign themselves up. Regional registration goes through a teacher login. The provincial rule document at skillscanada.bc.ca/competitions/rules-and-regulations/ lists exact eligibility. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: Volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: Only 16 and older. Younger teens should look at the Austin Public Library youth volunteer program (ages 13 to 17).

name: Burke Composite Squadron, Civil Air Patrol cadets
org: Civil Air Patrol, Virginia Wing (Burke Composite Squadron)
pay_detail: Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the pages read.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursday nights 6:30 to 9:00
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time. Email the squadron to ask about visiting a meeting.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 (the Virginia Wing page says to be at least 12 and not yet 19, and a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). The squadron has both teen and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email va-130info@vawg.cap.gov or call (703) 239-4530 to ask about a meeting. The Virginia Wing steps are to visit with your parents. Then go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the cadet application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Meetings are at Irving Middle School, 8100 Old Keene Mill, Springfield, VA 22152, but the location can change for school events, and in August they meet elsewhere. Meetings are cancelled on the same days Fairfax County Schools cancels. The squadron page says it won a 2021 Virginia Wing Squadron of Merit award.

name: American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State)
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.
who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 24 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: Youth Employment Opportunity Program (YEOP)
city: California (YEOP specialists at local EDD offices)
pay_detail: No pay. The page does not say whether services cost anything.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No application dates. Contact a YEOP specialist any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.

name: EDD Employment Services for Youth (America's Job Centers of California)
city: California (local America's Job Center of California offices)
pay_detail: The services are free (the page says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost). Work experience can be paid or unpaid; no pay rate is given.
duration: Ongoing, set by each local center
deadline_text: No application dates. Visit or contact your local center any time.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page read; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Volunteers Youth Service Corps
org: California Volunteers (Office of the Governor), run through partner cities and counties
city: California (23 partner cities, counties and tribes)
regions: los-angeles; oakland; sacramento; san-francisco; san-jose; orange-county; inland-empire; san-diego
pay_detail: At least minimum wage; the rate varies by location (page wording).
duration: Not stated on the state page; set by each local program
deadline_text: The state page does not say whether applications are open. Each partner city or county runs its own application.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: Next-Gen Manufacturing Academy (High School Summer Academy)
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
duration: Club year
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.
who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the 4-H page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

name: California Cadet Corps (school based leadership program)
org: California Cadet Corps, California Military Department
grades: Grades 4 to 12 per the program site; the state military page says grades 6 to 12
pay_detail: Free. The program site says it is fully funded by the state with no cost to families or host schools. Cadets earn up to ten elective credits per year.
duration: Ongoing school year program
deadline_text: No dates. Enrollment follows your school's schedule.
who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages read do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Pages read did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.

name: California FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
city: California (through school chapters in six geographic sections)
grades: Not stated on the pages read
pay_detail: Not a job. The join page lists no dues amounts.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline on the page.
who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: The CDE page lists no student application dates. Each school sets its own.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy sets its own application. Search the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Capital Area NextGen Youth Services
org: Capital Area Workforce Development Board (NCWorks Career Centers)
pay_detail: Apprenticeships and work experience are listed as services. Whether work experience is paid is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or enrollment status. Use the Complete an Interest Form button.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 in Wake and Johnston counties per the Capital Area youth page. The NextGen site says the program serves young adults facing barriers such as legal issues, home problems or missed education, and lists Wake, Johnston, Chatham, Lee and Orange counties. Exact eligibility rules and income limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form for your county at capitalareanextgen.org, or use the Request More Information form on the Capital Area youth page.
notes: This is the federal workforce (WIOA) style youth program for Wake County. Durham is covered by a different workforce board and is not listed. The pages do not say whether 14 to 17 year olds qualify in every case; ask the career center.

name: Cassadaga Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: College Preview (pre-college art and design program)
pay_detail: Commuter $3,000 total ($2,750 tuition and fees plus a $250 registration fee). Residential $3,600 total (adds $600 room and board). Scholarships available.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
deadline_text: 2026 session: registration opened Nov 3, 2025, scholarship applications closed April 27, 2026, registration closed May 11, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12) interested in art and design.
how_to_apply: Register online and pay the $250 registration fee. Scholarship applicants submit a form, a 300 to 500 word personal statement, three artwork samples and a NACAC fee waiver.
notes: Fees shown are the 2026 prices. Meals are included on weekdays. Refunds: tuition balance less the registration fee is refunded in full if withdrawn by June 15, 2026 and half by June 29, 2026.

name: Supporting Student Success (WIOA In-School Youth)
org: Contra Costa County Office of Education
city: Contra Costa County, CA (West County and East County)
pay_detail: Paid workforce prep and work experience (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Ongoing
who_can_apply: High school students who meet at least one criterion, such as low income, foster youth, system-involved, homeless, pregnant or parenting, English learner, below grade level in math or reading, or an IEP.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Referral Form (online form linked on the CCCOE page) or call: West County (925) 296-1507 or 296-1504; East County (925) 296-1505 or 296-1506.
notes: The out-of-school program is for ages 18 to 24, so only the in-school program fits most teens. Help can include transportation, interview clothes and school supplies.

name: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
org: CDC David J. Sencer Museum (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
city: Atlanta, GA (CDC headquarters, in person day camp)
grades: Students entering junior or senior year (high school sophomores and juniors during the application year)
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to attend. Campers cover their own housing and daily transportation.
duration: Five days, 8:45 AM to 4:00 PM. The 2026 sessions were June 22 to 26 and July 20 to 24.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for 2027 summer program information.
who_can_apply: High school students in the summer before junior or senior year, at least 16 on the first day of camp (no exceptions). A government photo ID is needed for CDC security. Non-Atlanta residents may apply but must arrange housing and travel. Non-U.S. citizens may apply with the documents asked for.
how_to_apply: The pages read do not describe the application steps. The camp page says the application is found through the FAQ page when it opens, and to check back in January 2027.
notes: Very competitive in past years, but numbers were not on the pages read. Sessions are fixed, campers cannot arrive late, leave early or miss days.

name: Cedars-Sinai Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers buy the required volunteer jacket for $30 (cash) and wear black or white scrubs.
duration: Winter/Spring and Fall: one 2-hour shift a week for 10 weeks (20 hours). Summer: two 4-hour shifts a week for 5 weeks (40 hours).
deadline_text: 2027 sessions: Winter/Spring (Jan 25 to Apr 4) applications Nov 23, 2026; Summer (Jun 21 to Jul 25) applications Mar 29, 2027; Fall (Oct 4 to Dec 12) applications Aug 2, 2027. First come, first served; each application closes when spots fill.
who_can_apply: Students 14 to 18 enrolled in high school with a transcript showing at least a 3.2 GPA. New volunteers and one parent or guardian must attend a mandatory in-person Teen Information Session.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with your transcript, finish the online volunteer orientation, complete health screening and flu vaccine (flu season Nov 1 to Apr 30), and attend the Teen Information Session (Monday, Jan 11, 2027, 5:30 to 7:00 p.m.).
notes: Spots are limited and fill fast, so apply the day the window opens. Shifts run Monday to Sunday. Teens who want research should look at Cedars-Sinai's separate INSPIRE Internship Program (not checked here). Questions: TeenVolunteerProgram@cshs.org or 310-423-8044.

name: Chabot College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.
duration: Per term
deadline_text: Rolling by term.
who_can_apply: Current high school students. Each semester you complete a Chabot application and the concurrent enrollment packet. You can take any class except basic skills and PE.
how_to_apply: Apply to Chabot, pick a class, complete the IDE Enrollment Form, then register through MyPortal. Questions: cc-earlycollege@chabotcollege.edu or 510-723-6701.
notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.

name: Galaxy Explorers Program
grades: Typically enters the summer before 10th grade and stays through 12th grade
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
deadline_text: Applications open each year from February 1 to March 31. Decisions in early May, orientation early to mid June. The page does not list 2027 dates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated, so needs_work_permit is null.

name: Carle Foundation Hospital Student Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: By term (fall, spring, summer)
deadline_text: Applications are due by 5 p.m. on August 29 (fall term), November 15 (spring term) or April 15 (summer term). The page gives no year.
who_can_apply: High school volunteers must be 14 or older. Students must provide up-to-date immunization records.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button under 'Students (college/teen)' on the Carle Foundation Hospital volunteer page (opens an online application) and send immunization records.
notes: The next listed deadline is the spring term deadline of November 15; confirm the year and current rules with Carle Volunteer Services. Other Carle sites list their own teen age ranges.

name: Youth Services (Workforce Development)
pay_detail: Not stated for youth. A separate Work Experience page says qualified interns can have up to 240 hours of wages covered.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: None stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who meet at least one condition, such as low family income, a disability, being a school dropout, homeless or foster youth, or needing extra help to finish school or get a job.
how_to_apply: The page gives no workNet address or walk-in hours. General CCRPC office: 1776 E Washington St, Urbana, IL 61802, (217) 328-3313.
notes: Eligibility rules apply, so not every teen qualifies. Call to ask about summer paid placements. The workforce site may be updated separately at eciwork.net. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: Counselor-in-Training, Summer Day Camps
pay_detail: Volunteer position.
duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
deadline_text: No application dates posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17. Candidates are picked through an application and interview.
how_to_apply: Email or call Stacey Clementz at the Homer Lake Interpretive Center, (217) 896-2455, or use the online volunteer application on the page.
notes: Youth program volunteers (school programs, September to May) and public program volunteers are also listed on the page; age rules for those are not stated. The District also has public volunteer events that need no application.

name: Champaign Park District Seasonal and Summer Jobs
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.
duration: Seasonal jobs run April to November and do not exceed 6 months; summer camp is a 10-week program
deadline_text: No application dates or deadlines listed on the page.
who_can_apply: The page says 15 year olds can apply for lifeguard and swim instructor. Minimum ages for other jobs are not stated; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the District's job listings (linked from the Employment Opportunities page). Aquatics questions: Ryan Hays, ryan.hays@champaignparks.org. HR: hr@champaignparks.org.
notes: Lifeguard classes are run by the District in Champaign-Urbana. Concession workers get a paid-for Food Handler's certification. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: Champaign Park District Teen Volunteering
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteers register on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal.
who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 years old who are enthusiastic, hardworking and willing to learn. Teen volunteers may work at most 25 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal, then view opportunities. Questions: volunteer@champaignparks.org.
notes: Some roles (for example Prairie Farm) run only part of the year.

name: Dual Credit and Dual Enrollment at Parkland College
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask the Early College office.
who_can_apply: At least 15 years old, attending an area high school or home-schooled, with course prerequisites and assessment requirements met. For high school credit you also need your school's approval and good standing.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply page under Dual Credit. Early College Services: 217-353-2663, earlycollege@parkland.edu (office U214).
notes: Early College students do not qualify for financial aid. Credit and grades go on a permanent Parkland transcript. The Early College page also lists an Early College and Career Academy with programs such as Automotive Technology, Certified Nurse Assistant and EMS.

name: Champaign Public Library Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Typically 2 to 3 hours a week; a 4-month minimum is preferred
deadline_text: No deadline.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. If you are 16 or 17 you need a signed waiver from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application, then schedule the required interview. Contact: Eva Liu, Volunteer Coordinator, volunteer@champaign.org, 217-403-2000 x3.
notes: Open roles change, so look at the current listings on the page. The Douglass Branch's Club Fred program is a summer role.

name: Grainger Engineering Summer Camps
grades: Rising 7th to 12th grade. Individual camps have narrower ranges, such as 7th to 9th or 10th to 12th.
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $1,500, commuter $750, day camp $550, each plus a $25 deposit. The Trail Blazer Scholarship covers 50% or 100% for students who meet its criteria.
duration: One week per camp (June to August in 2026)
deadline_text: All 2026 camps are listed as full. 2027 application dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Pre-college students entering the listed grades in the fall. The page does not mention international students.
how_to_apply: Camp application (with the scholarship application inside it). See the Camp FAQs for the process.
notes: Costs do not include travel to campus. Some camps are EAGER or IDEA camps focused on broadening participation, open to all to apply. Use the WYSE mailing list for next year's dates.

name: Young Scholars STEMM Research Program
pay_detail: No cost except transportation. Housing, meals and a monetary award are provided (the page calls it a fellowship payment; the amount is not stated).
duration: 6 weeks (research began June 17 and ended July 31 in 2026); 30 to 35 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications Closed for Summer 2026.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who live in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa or Wisconsin. No international applicants. No course prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Online application with student information, two personal statements and a teacher, mentor or counselor recommendation form (emailed after you submit). Join the Summer Program Notifications mailing list for next year's dates.
notes: Competitive: applications are ranked together, not first come first served. Housing is for selected students who do not live locally. Students get no course credit.

name: Counselor-in-Training (CIT) Program
pay_detail: No wage is listed on the page; it is described as training for future summer and part-time jobs. Confirm with the contact.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week, three days a week, June 3 to July 31 in 2026 (8:15 am to 3 pm)
deadline_text: 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who have completed 7th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application (PDF or online form on the Teen Programs page). Questions: Cathy Schneider (contact link on the page).
notes: Because pay is not stated, ask whether CITs are paid before applying. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

name: FRESH Crew Teen Volunteer Days
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn service hours and references.
duration: 2 hours per event (2 to 4 pm Saturdays)

name: Youth Event Support Volunteer

deadline_text: No deadline stated.

how_to_apply: Read the position descriptions, then fill out the volunteer interest form on the library's Volunteer with us page and pick Youth Event Support Volunteer.
notes: The 14 to 17 range comes from the age options on the interest form, not from a written rule. Call 919-968-2777 or email library@chapelhillnc.gov to confirm the minimum age and hours. The library also has a Teen Room for ages 13 to 18; no teen advisory board was listed on the pages read.

name: Youth Volunteer Shifts (Blue Ridge Area Food Bank, Charlottesville)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts
duration: One shift at a time. Shift length is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for shifts on the online volunteer calendar. Group visits must be booked at least one month ahead.
who_can_apply: Children ages 12 to 17 may volunteer if a parent or guardian is with them for each shift. In the Food Recovery Area, ages 12 to 16 need a parent or guardian at each shift. Volunteers ages 17 and older may work there without an adult after an initial shift with an adult. Youth groups ages 12 to 15 need one adult chaperone for every 3 children. Youth groups ages 16 and 17 need one adult for every 6 youth. Volunteers must be 18 or older at the Winchester warehouse.
how_to_apply: Create your own account on the online volunteer calendar. It is required for safety and communication. Then register for a shift. If you do not get a confirmation email, the registration did not go through. Contact the volunteer team at volunteer@brafb.org. Group sizes are 4 to 8 people at most locations. They are up to 10 at the Verona warehouse. Everyone needs their own account.
notes: A parent or guardian must be at every shift for ages 12 to 17, so this works best for families. The page lists the front desk as (540) 268-3663. The footer lists 540-248-3663. Confirm which number is right. The page we read names the Winchester and Verona warehouses. It does not name the Charlottesville warehouse. Confirm which age rule applies there.

name: Junior Volunteers (Charlottesville-Albemarle SPCA)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The volunteer pays a $25 volunteer fee plus a separate $9 background check. The page does not say if either is refundable.
duration: Ongoing. Hours and length are not stated.

how_to_apply: Use the Schedule Orientation or Volunteer Application link on the SPCA volunteer page to choose an orientation date and fill out the volunteer application. Orientation comes before you take on tasks. Contact: volunteer@caspca.org or 434-973-5959 ext. 314.
notes: The pages do not say if 14 to 17 year olds need a parent signature. They do not say if there are limits on which animals teens can work with. Ask at orientation. The apply link goes to the SPCA's event calendar on a third party site.

name: CATEC Career and Technical Programs (Charlottesville Area Technical Education Center)
org: Charlottesville Area Technical Education Center (CATEC), run by Charlottesville City Schools
grades: Not stated on the pages read

They are Biology II, English 12, USA Government, and Economics and Personal Finance. EMT and Fire Science are no longer dual enrollment through CVCC. Students still earn CTE credits. Address: 1000 East Rio Road, Charlottesville.

name: Community Attention Youth Internship Program (CAYIP)
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
deadline_text: The page lists four school-year sessions and one summer session for 2026-27 but gives dates only for Fall 2026 (applications Aug 20-28, 2026, now closed). For reference, the Summer 2025 application window was April 1 to May 1, 2025 (5 pm).
who_can_apply: Charlottesville-area youth 14 to 21 (14 by the start of the CAYIP Academy). City of Charlottesville residents get priority. Parent or guardian must also complete paperwork for youth under 18.
how_to_apply: Submit the CAYIP application (questionnaire, inventory and agreement to participate) during the session window, then a one-on-one interview. Accepted youth attend the mandatory paid CAYIP Academy. Contact: cayipinquiries@charlottesville.gov, 434-987-0018.
notes: Applications are only accepted during a session window. Transportation is not provided. Interns may miss at most 5 days per session. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers must get an Employment Certificate before any work; the program page does not mention it, so ask CAYIP staff how it is handled.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Monticello Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Monticello Composite Squadron (Virginia Wing)
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

notes: Confirm first: the squadron page gives no street address, so ask for the exact meeting location before you go. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: Lifeguard Training (Charlottesville Parks and Recreation)
org: City of Charlottesville Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Session dates were not listed on the page; use the Registration & Tickets link.
who_can_apply: Listed for ages 15 and up. Everyone must pass the in-water pretest or be removed from the class.
how_to_apply: Register through the city's Registration & Tickets system. Within 72 hours of registering, email swimprograms@charlottesville.gov with the subject Lifeguard Pretest to book the pretest at least 8 days ahead.
notes: The page does not say the class leads to a job. The city lists seasonal and variable-hour jobs on governmentjobs.com; none were open on 2026-10-09. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before any work.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
pay_detail: The program page does not mention pay or a stipend. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around pay.

deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: Re-read on 2026-10-09: ages 13 to 15, Chicago residence, the apply step (contact the park) and the 2026 session dates all match the page. The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. It does not mention pay, so the pay type was changed from stipend to no pay stated. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site. Use the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page. Or go to a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the CHP post page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.

name: 10x10 Teen Volunteer Team (Cincinnati Art Museum)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer team

who_can_apply: Volunteer team applicants should be in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer team form linked on the 10x10 Teen Art Expo page when applications open. Teen artists (age and grade rules for artists are not stated) can submit art when submissions open in mid November 2026. Museum phone: 513-721-2787.
notes: The museum has other volunteer groups. They are docents, visitor service aides, REC volunteers and CAM Cruiser volunteers. The main volunteer page does not state ages for them. Ask the museum before applying to those.

name: Teen Workforce Development (Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati
pay_detail: Free. The summer and school year programs are listed as completely free. The page does not say that teens are paid.

deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Enroll through the Club member portal.

how_to_apply: Click Enroll Today on the Join the Clubs page (it goes to the Club portal), or contact your preferred Club for help with the application. After acceptance, families get any extra forms. Phone: 513-421-8909. Email: info@bgcgc.org. Main office: 1205 Dewey Ave., Cincinnati, OH 45205.
notes: Confirm first. The pages do not list teen ages, teen hours, or any teen jobs. No Junior Staff program is mentioned. Clubs are at Price Hill, Avondale, Eastgate and East Westwood in Ohio. They are at Newport and Covington in Kentucky. There is also a Western & Southern Workforce Development Center.

name: High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
deadline_text: The deadline for the Summer 2026 session has passed. The page says the summer application is usually posted in January, with about two months to finish the packet.
who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade. Seniors still in high school in spring must use the high school application.
how_to_apply: Submit the application packet by the posted due date, then attend a parent information session, an in-person interview and an orientation. Medical screening and a background check are required.
notes: Competitive: only the highest scoring applicants are accepted. Volunteers must complete at least 80 percent of their scheduled shifts. The hospital does not arrange job shadowing or senior capstone hours through Volunteer Services.

name: Aquatics Jobs: Lifeguard and Pool Staff
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page. A 2026 lifeguard screening registration form is linked.
who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older, hold current American Red Cross Lifeguard Training/First Aid and CPR for the Professional Rescuer/AED certifications, and pass a water skills test. The page does not give an age for gate or pool monitors.
how_to_apply: Register for the required lifeguard course screening on the page, then apply to the open positions. Questions: CRC Aquatics, 513-357-7665.
notes: Lifeguards also attend pre-season and on-site pool training and pass an annual water skills review. Check the page for current screening dates. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Youth to Work (Y2WK) Summer Jobs
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the pages read
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
deadline_text: The program page says the application is usually available February to March. In 2026 the deadline passed in March (WVXU reported about two weeks left on March 10, 2026). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Live in the City of Cincinnati or a surrounding community and be 14 to 24. A limited number of positions are for ages 14 and 15. Under 18, a parent or guardian signs the hiring forms; under 16 you need a work permit.
how_to_apply: Create a free account at governmentjobs.com, then apply to the Y2WK job at agency.governmentjobs.com/cincinnati. Only online applications are accepted. Applicants are contacted by phone or email for an interview.
notes: Very competitive: WVXU reported more than 1,000 teens applied last year and about 6 percent were hired. The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Teen Volunteers (Great Parks of Hamilton County)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Long term volunteering. Time commitment is not stated on the page.

notes: Confirm first: the page gives no teen application steps or time commitment. Great Parks also lists one day volunteer projects; the page read did not state a minimum age for them.

name: Library Volunteer Opportunities (ages 12+)

how_to_apply: Fill in an application in the library's online volunteer system and pick a listing. Questions: 513-369-6968.
notes: Each branch listing sets its own details, so check the age on the listing you choose. The page also mentions meal-service and tutoring roles. It lists a separate Friends of the Library volunteer line at 513-369-6035.

name: Youth Programs Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
deadline_text: Youth volunteers are recruited each year from January through March. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, from public, private, parochial, charter and homeschool backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Use the youth application link on the Youth Programs page when recruitment opens. Email youthprograms@cincymuseum.org to be notified.
notes: The program started in 1989. In the first summer teens shadow the Museum of Natural History and Science, The Children's Museum and the Cincinnati History Museum.

name: Youth Volunteer Opportunities (Cincinnati Nature Center)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application linked on the Youth Volunteer Opportunities page when recruiting reopens. Questions: volunteer@cincynature.org or (513) 965-3348. The youth opportunities page lists the main phone as (513) 831-1711.
notes: The pages read do not give the street address. Check the Nature Center site for the location. Group service days, including for local high schools, remove invasive plants. The youth opportunities page we read says ages 13 to 18 may apply. It did not repeat the closed for 2026 wording. Check the status before you plan around it.

name: Green Team Youth Summer Jobs

notes: Work sites named by the City include Mt. Echo Park, Mt. Airy Forest, Mt. Storm, Caldwell Nature Preserve and Kennedy Heights Park. Pay, hours and the application window are not on the pages, so ask Groundwork ORV. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Job Shadowing (TriHealth)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned on the page.
duration: Typically about 8 to 16 hours (varies by department or unit)
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted. Check with the program.

how_to_apply: Email one message to job_shadows@trihealth.com. Include these items. The Job Shadow Instructions. Your Application. The Risk and Release form. The Authorization to Treat Minors form. Your immunization records. The team does not match you to a department. Look at TriHealth's services and locations first.
notes: The TriHealth volunteer page says Good Samaritan and Bethesda North hospitals use adult and teen volunteers. It does not give a teen age or steps. Email volunteer@trihealth.com or call 513-862-2368 to ask. The job shadowing page does not mention a background check.

name: Early IT Summer Camp (University of Cincinnati)
org: University of Cincinnati School of Information Technology
pay_detail: Free to attend. A light breakfast and lunch are provided each day. No pay.
duration: Three weeks, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The page lists June 1 to June 18 and does not print the year.
deadline_text: The camp page says registration is open and that the camp is first come, first served and spots fill up fast. It does not print a deadline or the year, so confirm the dates with the Early IT team.
who_can_apply: High school students from rising 9th grade through rising 12th grade who like technology. In person camp only, and only domestic students are accepted right now.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Here link on the Early IT Summer Camp page. Tell them in your application if cost or lack of resources could keep you from taking part. Questions: ucearlyit@ucmail.uc.edu. There is a parent or guardian orientation on Zoom.
notes: Drop off is at Teacher-Dyer Complex, Room 160 (University Circle), between 8:30 and 10 a.m. with pick up 4:00 to 4:30 p.m. The FAQ says the camp runs over two weeks in one answer and the page says three weeks, so confirm the length.

name: Medical Sciences Summer Institute (University of Cincinnati)
org: University of Cincinnati College of Medicine
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors
pay_detail: $1,100 (2026 price). A limited number of scholarships and financial aid awards are available.
duration: One week per session, Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. In 2026 there were five sessions between June 1 and June 26.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are 16 or older by August 1 of the program year (in 2026 that date was August 1, 2026). Previous research experience is not required.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application form. You also upload a 1 page resume style summary of your school work and activities. You upload a 1 page personal statement. You rank the session you prefer. Contact: Michele Glassmeyer, Michele.Glassmeyer@uc.edu, (513) 558-6351.
notes: Costs money. The price, session dates and age cutoff above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.

name: ZooTeen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application is open online Dec 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027. Information sessions Nov 16, Dec 14 and Jan 11 (6 to 7 p.m.). Group interviews Feb 27, Feb 28, Mar 13 or Mar 14. Decisions by email April 2, 2027.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. The page words the age rule as 13 to 17 on May 1, 2026, which looks like a leftover date for a 2027 season, so confirm.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with essays, attend one group interview and two orientations, and set up an online profile to log hours.
notes: Orientation 1 is an online course with a guardian plus a session on April 24 or 25, 2027; Orientation 2 is all day at the Zoo on May 22 or 23, 2027. The Zoo says to contact them if the fee is a hardship. Third-year and older ZooTeens have a lower 70 hour requirement.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (California Wing)
org: Civil Air Patrol, California Wing (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
city: California (squadrons in eight regional groups, Los Angeles to San Diego)
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available.
duration: Ongoing; weekly squadron meetings
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend about three meetings, then complete the application.

how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (Georgia Wing)
org: Civil Air Patrol, Georgia Wing (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
city: Georgia (squadrons across the state; wing office at Dobbins Air Reserve Base, Marietta, GA)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, per the national page. A very active cadet might spend about $300 to $600 in the first year before aid, with some help for uniforms and overnight fees.

deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron and attend at least three meetings.

how_to_apply: Find a local squadron with the Georgia Wing locator. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application, or ask if you can apply online. Wing office: 770-428-9031, publicaffairs@gawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Georgia Wing page says cadets are not obligated to join the military. The national page lists military obligation for cadets as none. Dues vary by location and the national page says $25 to $50 per year, so ask your squadron for the exact amount. The Georgia Wing home page lists squadrons including Atlanta (GA109), Marietta, Roswell, Chamblee, Lawrenceville, Cumming and others.

name: FARMS Leadership Program

deadline_text: No dates posted. Schools sign up as groups.

notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.

Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: College Park Composite Squadron, Civil Air Patrol cadets

notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Squadron location: 6709 Corporal Frank Scott Drive, College Park, MD 20740. Commander listed on the page: Capt. Estelle Roche, estelle.roche@mdwg.cap.gov. The meeting time is from the squadron page; confirm before you go.

name: Shakespeare in the Parks Apprenticeship Program

name: Teen Arts Council (Prince George's County Parks and Recreation)

how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is free. It has a short essay and a piece of original artwork in your preferred genre, such as music, dance or visual arts. Contact: Shaiday Dancy, Teen Arts Specialist, 301-446-3252, shaiday.dancy@pgparks.com.
notes: Applicants could also be invited to be a Teen Arts Council ambassador. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

name: Discovering Engineering (University of Maryland)
org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering
pay_detail: $1,400 per student (project materials, activities, and room and board; transportation is not included). Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.
duration: One week, residential. In 2026: Session One July 26 to 31 and Session Two August 2 to 7 (you attend one).
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was April 24, 2026, with notices by May 15. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade in the fall. The page does not list a GPA or location rule.

notes: Costs money. Price, dates and deadline above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.

name: Pre-College Scholars Program (University of Maryland)
org: University of Maryland, A. James Clark School of Engineering
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (currently in 10th or 11th grade)
pay_detail: The whole program costs $400 per student. Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.
duration: Three weeks, in person on the UMD campus. The 2026 session ran Monday July 6 to Friday July 24.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday May 8, 2026, with notices by May 22 and rolling spots after that. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students who go to high school in Maryland or Washington, D.C., or live there. You need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5. You must show interest and skill in math, science or engineering.
how_to_apply: Online application with a one page personal statement (12 point, double spaced), an official high school transcript, and official PSAT or SAT scores if you have them. You must attend all sessions, orientation, and the pre and post tests. Contact: Ms. Aishah Briscoe, FutureEngineer@umd.edu.
notes: The page does not say whether the program is residential. Costs money but is low compared with most pre-college programs. Dates and the $400 price are from the 2026 page.

name: SPARC Robotics Certificate Program (University of Maryland)
org: Maryland Robotics Center, University of Maryland
pay_detail: The Summer 2026 price was $5,000 for one 3 week session (project materials and activities; lunch and transportation are not included). The 2027 price is not posted. A limited number of need based scholarships are available, and payments are not refundable.
