Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.

name: Edison Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: High School Scholars Program, Middlesex College
pay_detail: $150 per course plus textbooks for in-county residents; students from other counties, states or countries pay the out-of-county rate (not listed).
duration: Courses of 3 to 4 credits; up to 8 credits per semester
deadline_text: No deadline listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 who are at least 15 years old.
how_to_apply: Download the application and email it to k12partnerships@middlesexcollege.edu, or call 732-906-2554 to schedule a virtual appointment.
notes: Separate Dual Enrollment: in participating districts, college courses are taught at the high school. Ask your counselor.

name: Teen Advisory Board (TAB), Edison Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Monthly meetings
deadline_text: Monthly. The listing shows the next session as Wednesday, October 14, 7:00 to 8:30 p.m., Main Library Children's Room.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Registration required.
how_to_apply: Register on the library event listing (registration required). Meetings alternate between the Main Library and the North Edison Branch; members may attend at either. Main Library: 340 Plainfield Avenue, Edison, 732-287-2298.
notes: The page I read did not print a year for the October 14 session, and the library's own Young Adults page had no volunteer details. Confirm the meeting location when you register.

name: El Camino Health Junior Auxiliary
city: Mountain View and Los Gatos, CA
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 1 year
deadline_text: No application deadline posted. The page says to check back in mid-January 2027 for signup for the next Junior Application Seminar.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. Competitive, with limited spots. No summer-only option.
how_to_apply: Attend the annual application seminar, then apply. Info on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Hospital does not offer summer-only or programs shorter than one year. Locations are Mountain View and Los Gatos. Spots are limited (earlier check).

name: Elk Grove Youth Commission
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers
deadline_text: No open recruitment as of Oct 7, 2026. Seats are filled when openings come up, and the City posts a notice with a Youth Commission application.
who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages read, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City page returned HTTP 403, so it could not be read again and the card stays snippet-only.

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program (Emory Healthcare)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No program fee stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks (June 1 to July 24 in 2026), one shift per week, Monday to Thursday, at least 4 hours
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened Feb 17 and closed Feb 27, 2026 (or earlier if full). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 as of June 1 of the program year (June 1, 2026 on the current page).
how_to_apply: Create a MyImpact account and complete the application, with student and parent signatures on four forms. Get a recommendation from a teacher or school counselor by the deadline and rank up to three hospital locations. Interview, health screening and orientation follow.
notes: The window was only 10 days in 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting in early 2027. Space is limited and waitlists happen. Health screening includes a TB test and proof of chickenpox and measles immunity. No shadowing, internships or clinical hours.

name: Emory Pre-College Program
pay_detail: 2026 prices: 2-week noncredit course $5,510 residential or $3,925 commuter; 3-week institute $8,264 residential; 4 weeks $11,020. $70 application fee. 2027 prices not posted.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks (2027 noncredit sessions June 13 to 26, June 27 to July 10, July 11 to 24)
deadline_text: Applications for 2027 open in December 2026. Deadlines: noncredit sessions May 3, 2027; Pre-Med Institute Feb 1, 2027; credit Summer College April 20 and June 7, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students; the page says it serves current sophomores and juniors. Application needs transcript and recommendations.
how_to_apply: Choose a program and course, review costs, then start the online application (transcript, recommendations, $70 fee). After acceptance, complete the pre-arrival checklist and pay the $350 enrollment deposit.
notes: Expensive. The nearest deadline is the Pre-Med Institute on Feb 1, 2027 (deadline_iso shows the main May 3 date). Financial aid deadline was May 1 in 2026. Information sessions are in November and December 2026.

name: Evergreen Valley College Dual Enrollment and CCAP
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.
who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED, with approval from your school counselor or principal. Adult school students in GED programs can also join.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.

name: Exploring (Learning for Life career posts)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.
duration: Meets regularly
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line. apply_url is the joinexploring.org home page, which has an Enter ZIP Code box for Exploring posts and clubs near you. On exploring.org, the Council Locator heading links to the contact page, and the scouting.org Local Council Locator finds a council, not a unit.

name: High School Internships (Facciotti Lab)
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.
deadline_text: No application process or dates posted.
who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.

name: Lifeguard jobs with free training
pay_detail: Weekday opening and midday shifts start at $15.00 per hour; weekday evenings and weekends range from $12.41 to $15.00 per hour. Training is free (listed as a $250 value).
duration: Part-time; hours vary by Rec Center
deadline_text: Open positions posted on the page; no deadline stated. Training dates are shared at the interview.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 15 at the start of the course. Must pass the lifeguard course and its swim prerequisites (swim 100 yards, retrieve a 10-pound brick, tread water without hands for one minute) and a criminal background check. No prior certification needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Park Authority Aquatic Certification page, then interview. Questions: FCPAJOBS@Fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Employment is contingent on passing the course. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page read does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Fairfax County Public Library volunteering (youth 12 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: The library's volunteer guide is for adults, youth ages 12 and over, corporate groups, and people who need to fulfill a service requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator for your branch (the guide lists names and phone numbers) or use the Volunteer Login link in the library's volunteering guide.
notes: The guide does not spell out the sign-up steps for teens, so call your branch coordinator first. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Educating Youth through Employment (EYE) summer program
org: Fairfax County Department of Family Services Workforce Development and Virginia Career Works Northern Region
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate is not stated on the pages read.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: The 2026 program ended with a recognition ceremony on Aug 14, 2026. The county says employer recruitment for the next summer begins in spring 2027. Youth sign-up dates for 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. You must be legally allowed to work in the U.S. You must be getting services from a referring group or the WIOA Youth Program. You must want to find work. You must be able to work at least 20 hours a week and go to the workshops.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply alone. A sponsoring group or the WIOA Youth Program picks you. Email DFSEYE@fairfaxcounty.gov or see vcwnorthern.com/eye-programs/ to find a referring organization.
notes: Referral only. The county page also lists a WIOA Youth program for ages 17 to 24 who are out of school or close to graduating. In summer 2026, 133 youth worked with 100 local employers. Virginia work permit rules were not checked.

name: AI in Health Summer Camp (George Mason University)
org: George Mason University, Department of Health Administration and Policy
pay_detail: The camps list at Mason says it is a free, five day program. The camp page itself does not list a cost.
duration: 5 days, 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. each day
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran July 27 to 31, 2026 and applications are closed. No 2027 dates are posted. The page offers a Future Programs Interest Form.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students. No coding, health care or technology experience is required.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Fill out the Future Programs Interest Form on the camp page to get updates. Contact: Maria Uriyo, muriyo@gmu.edu.
notes: This is a day camp at George Mason University's Fairfax campus, 4400 University Drive, Fairfax, VA 22030. Not a job.

name: VALHEN STEM Academy (George Mason University)
org: George Mason University College of Science, STEM Academy
grades: Rising high school juniors (current 10th graders when applying)
pay_detail: Free for selected students. Overnight students get two nights of dorm housing, meals and a daily snack. A limited number of day-only slots exist. You arrange your own transportation.
duration: 3 days, 2 nights
deadline_text: The 2027 program is tentatively July 28 to 30, 2027, with final dates confirmed in January 2027. The application opens in February 2027. No deadline is posted yet.
who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The program page itself says rising juniors, so use the program page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.

name: Future Women Leaders in Law Enforcement (Fairfax County Police)
pay_detail: Free of charge. Transportation help is offered case by case.
duration: Summer weekdays
deadline_text: The page says the 2026 class has graduated and to check back next year for 2027 session information. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school age girls in Northern Virginia (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: For girls only. Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to go to all classes. Not a job.

name: Fairfax County Police Public Safety Cadets
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs for uniforms or gear are not stated on the page.
duration: Ongoing unit membership
deadline_text: The 2026 First Nighter meetings were Sept 1 to 3, 2026 (one for each unit). The page asks you to fill out an interest form for updates on future First Nighter dates. No deadline for 2027 is posted.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 20 who like the idea of a career in law enforcement. There are four units. They are the Criminal Justice Academy (Chantilly), West Potomac High School, Annandale High School and South Lakes High School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Public Safety Cadets interest form on the page. The page also links an application. It links a waiver. It links a recommendation form. Email fcpdpsc@fairfaxcounty.gov with questions.
notes: An older Fairfax County police page called these units Explorer posts. They had the same unit numbers. That page no longer loads. Ask the cadet email about the current rules, such as citizenship, grades and costs. The page links an application, a waiver and a recommendation form.

name: Fairfax County Teen Police Academy
pay_detail: Free. Transportation help is offered case by case.
duration: Summer weekdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
deadline_text: The page says the 2026 class has graduated and to check back next year for 2027 session information. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Fairfax County high school age students (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Police Academy application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to attend all classes. Not a job.

name: Fermilab PRISM (Program for Research, Innovation, and STEM Mentorship)
grades: Rising high school senior (senior in 2027-28) or 2027 high school graduate
pay_detail: $500 per week stipend. Housing is not provided; transportation assistance is available.
duration: 4 weeks, July 12 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications open Jan 12, 2027 and close Mar 1, 2027 (recommendation letter also due Mar 1). Offers Apr 12, 2027; accept by Apr 21, 2027.
who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link. It is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the program page.

name: Fermilab VALOR JROTC Summer Internship
grades: Illinois JROTC high school junior, senior or recent graduate
pay_detail: $18 per hour. No onsite housing or transportation reimbursement.
duration: 6 weeks, June 28 to Aug 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications opened Oct 5, 2026 and close Feb 5, 2027. Offers Mar 15, 2027; accept by Mar 22, 2027.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.

name: Fernbank Youth Interpreters (FYI) Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time $50 fee after acceptance, which can be waived for those who qualify.
duration: One year, June 1 to May 31, at least 45 hours
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications are closed. The museum expects to post information on the 2027-28 program in February 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.

name: Trailblazers -N- Training
org: City of Folsom Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
deadline_text: 2026 post went up May 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.

name: Foothill College High School Dual Enrollment
city: Los Altos Hills and Sunnyvale, CA
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.
duration: One quarter at a time
deadline_text: No single deadline stated. Submit the form before you register each quarter.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).

name: Forage Virtual Job Simulations
pay_detail: Free
duration: Self-paced, usually a few hours
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.

name: Teen Corps
org: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)
duration: Summer program; length not stated
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 Teen Corps are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Eligible local teens. The page does not state the age range or other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Teen Corps page when it reopens. Contact the Teen Corps Coordinator through the page.
notes: Run on a community garden and the Conservatory's Farmers Market. Ages, stipend amount and dates are not on the page, so ask the coordinator. Ohio needs a working permit for paid work at ages 14 to 17, but 16 and 17 year olds do not need one for nonagricultural, nonhazardous work during summer vacation. See permit.html?state=oh for the steps.

name: Conservatory Volunteer Program (age 15+)
org: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: No minimum hours; weekly, monthly or seasonal
deadline_text: Opportunities are available year-round. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old and complete an application, a background check and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then complete the background check and orientation.
notes: Some outdoor roles run March to November and the Children's Garden runs April to October.

name: Fremont Unified Career and Technical Education
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
deadline_text: No dates stated. Choose courses at your school.
who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general. It lists 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. It does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.

name: Fremont Youth Advisory Commission
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

name: Teen Volunteers (Fulton County Library System)
org: Fulton County Library System (Atlanta-Fulton Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts after orientation
deadline_text: Applications are always accepted, but most projects are full and most locations have a waitlist.
who_can_apply: Youth under 18 may apply with a parent or guardian signature. The page does not state a minimum age, so ask Volunteer Services.
how_to_apply: Under 18: download and print the PDF application, sign it, get a parent or guardian signature, and return it to Volunteer Services by email, mail, fax or drop-off. Then attend orientation. Email vol.services@fultoncountyga.gov or call 404-613-0125.
notes: The page says the library is currently on hold for community service hour requirements, so students who need school hours must contact Volunteer Services early. Teen Advisory Boards exist at some branches; ask the Youth Services Librarian. Library Systems for DeKalb and Cobb counties are separate.

name: Work-Based Learning, Fulton County Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The district page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: Per school term
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator for the application window.
who_can_apply: Fulton County Schools students who are at least 16, in 11th or 12th grade, and following a defined career pathway. Individual schools may add rules. Students in Atlanta Public Schools use their own district.
how_to_apply: Print and finish the WBL Interest Form. Give it to your school's WBL coordinator. Students who meet the requirements are issued an application. Grades, attendance, discipline and related coursework are reviewed. You must follow up on job leads yourself.
notes: District contact listed on the page: Leslie McHann, 470-254-0466. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Teen Volunteers at Gail Borden Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
deadline_text: No deadline posted. A teen volunteer orientation is listed for Sunday, Oct 18, 1:00 to 1:30 PM at the Main Library Conference Room (the page does not print the year; Oct 18 is a Sunday in 2026).
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.
notes: Grade 6 is under 13, so younger readers should ask about their grade. The library's Elgin Teens page also describes Studio 270, a high school teen space at 270 N. Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.

name: Work-Based Learning (Internships), Gwinnett County Public Schools
pay_detail: School credit. The GCPS page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.
duration: One semester at a time as a school elective
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the district page. Forms go to your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator; ask when the next semester deadline is.
who_can_apply: Gwinnett County Public Schools juniors and seniors who are 16 by September 1 and have coursework that matches their career choice. The school reviews grades, attendance and discipline.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. Forms: electronic agreement, WBL application, recommendation form and job site information form. Forms are uploaded in the WBL class when the semester starts. Apprenticeships need a post-high-school plan.
notes: No home-office or private-residence placements. The program cannot guarantee a job. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Genesys Works Bay Area Internship Program
regions: east-bay; national; oakland; san-francisco; san-jose; silicon-valley
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
deadline_text: No dates posted. Applicants get an interview, then summer skills training.
who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages read. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.

name: Volunteens at Geneva Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
deadline_text: Fall 2026 session runs Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026. No registration deadline is listed. Dates for the next session are not posted.
who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.

name: Georgia 4-H
city: Georgia (county Extension offices statewide; state office in Athens, GA)
grades: Ages 8 to 18 (Senior Project Achievement is grades 9 to 12)
pay_detail: Not a job. The page says 4-H does not require a uniform or club fees. Camps and some activities may have their own costs, not listed on this page.
duration: Ongoing; clubs, projects, camps and conferences run through the year
deadline_text: No enrollment dates listed. Ask your county Extension office.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Cloverbud programs for ages 5 to 7 exist in some counties only.
how_to_apply: Contact your local county UGA Extension office, or Georgia 4-H at 706-542-4444 or ga4h@uga.edu. The site has a 'Find Your Local Club' page.
notes: The home page lists teen options. They are Ambassador Program, Leadership in Action, Step Up and Lead, Senior Conference, State Council and State Congress. The pages read did not give dates or ages for each. Check with the county office.

name: Teen Volunteer Program (Georgia Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid. $45 administrative fee (check or money order) once accepted. Perks: volunteer pass, free parking on shifts, 5 one-time daily tickets after finishing.
duration: 4 months per session: Spring (Jan to Apr) 60 hours, Summer (May to Aug) 80 hours, Fall (Sep to Dec) 60 hours
deadline_text: Spring 2027 session starts onboarding with information sessions in October 2026; dates not posted yet. The 2026 summer/fall cycle on the page: info sessions in July, application deadline Aug 1, interviews Aug 16, orientation Sept 12.
who_can_apply: High school or home school students ages 15 to 17 at the time of application. Teens need their own transportation and a parent or guardian must join the info session.
how_to_apply: Register for one mandatory virtual information session (email volunteer@georgiaaquarium.org or use the page's Contact Us interest form). A parent or guardian must attend with the teen. If chosen, attend a group interview. Bring birth certificate and photo ID.
notes: Not every applicant gets an interview. No behind-the-scenes roles for teens and no court-ordered or school service hours. The page lists the group interview as both three hours and four hours, and its weekday names for the 2026 dates do not match the calendar, so confirm exact dates with the Aquarium. Last-year dates are shown for reference only.

name: Georgia Boys State (American Legion)
pay_detail: Not a job. The 2026 memo says delegates pay a one time $5.00 'state tax' at registration. The sponsoring Legion post handles transportation. The page does not list a program fee.
duration: One week. 2026 session was June 7 to 13, 2026, about 400 delegates.
deadline_text: 2027 information is listed as 'coming soon'. The 2026 session ran June 7 to 13, 2026. The 2026 memo says the Samsung scholarship application was due online by the first day of the program.
who_can_apply: Male high school rising seniors. The home page says to contact your local American Legion Post or your Guidance Counselor for more information.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or school guidance counselor. Chosen students then use the 'Request to Attend' form. They also use a permission form. Both are on the Georgia Boys State site. Questions: administration@dogboysstate.org or 229-938-9352.
notes: Boys only (Girls State is a separate program run by the Auxiliary). The program is not a paid job, so no work permit. The 2026 memo says the week includes an evening devotional, and families who object may decline the invitation. Delegates must stay all week.

name: Georgia DECA
grades: Not stated on the pages read
pay_detail: Not a job. Student dues are $16 ($8 national and $8 state), per the state page.
duration: Membership is for one school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed. The state calendar lists a Fall Rally on October 21, 2026 at Six Flags Over Georgia.
who_can_apply: Students at a Georgia school with a DECA chapter. The state page does not list grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: The state page is written for school advisors. Chapters sign up and renew members online at deca.org. Ask a business or marketing teacher if your school has a chapter. A school can start one using the Start a Chapter page. The page says the Georgia DECA minimum is 15 members.
notes: Contact the state staff through the Contact Us page at gadeca.org.

name: Georgia FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
grades: Not stated on the page read
pay_detail: Not a job. Dues are not listed on the page read.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Georgia students interested in business careers. The home page does not list grade, age or dues.
how_to_apply: The page says 'Joining is simple!' and links a chapter finder to see which FBLA chapters are close to you. Students join through a local chapter.
notes: Ask your school whether it has an FBLA chapter. The page read does not list the state conference dates or dues.

name: Georgia FFA Association
org: Georgia FFA Association and Georgia Agricultural Education (Georgia Department of Education)
grades: Students enrolled in a Georgia agricultural education class (middle and high school)
pay_detail: Not a job. The membership page lists a yearly affiliation fee of $9.05 per high school student ($5.05 national, $4.00 state) and $900 per chapter for middle school. The page does not say whether families pay it.
duration: Ongoing during the school year
deadline_text: No membership deadline listed on the page. Enrollment follows your agriculture class schedule.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education classes at a Georgia school with an ag program. The membership page says every student in those classes becomes an FFA member.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an agricultural education class at your school. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. The state page says a student is expected to be in ag classes to join FFA.
notes: If your school has no ag program you cannot join through it. The state site links a 2026-2027 state agricultural education calendar for event dates.

name: Georgia Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Georgia
grades: Girls who have completed their junior year of high school
pay_detail: $350.00 registration fee, usually paid by the sponsoring unit or organization. The page says sponsors are listed for each girl.
duration: About one week. 2026 session was June 7 to 12, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: the 'I Want In' page said fee due April 20 and applications complete by May 20, 2026, while the Selection Criteria page said applications and fee due May 1, 2026. The two pages disagree, so plan for the earlier date and ask your unit. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Girls who finished junior year. You need high moral character and above-average school standing. An American Legion Auxiliary unit must sponsor you. Another group that a unit approves can sponsor you too. Each high school is limited to 12 girls.
how_to_apply: Contact the unit president or Girls State Chairman of a local American Legion Auxiliary unit. This is how you get sponsored. A selection committee picks the girls. Then the application is completed online. The school checks that you are eligible before school ends. Email georgiagirlsstate@gmail.com or call 678-289-8446.
notes: Girls only. The site shows 2026 dates and the 'I Want In' page says last updated 12/3/2022, so confirm with your unit before relying on the dates. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

name: Georgia Governor's Honors Program (GHP)
org: Georgia Governor's Office of Education, Workforce and Strategy (GOEWS)
city: Georgia (summer residential campus; host campus not named on the page read)
grades: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Free to apply. The page says required costs are travel to the semifinalist event and the host campus, basic supplies and optional spending money. Meals and rooms are provided.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July (residential)
deadline_text: Local school selection runs August to early November (ask your school's GHP Coordinator now). Then nominees get the online application link Nov 13, info session Dec 3, application due Jan 8, semifinalists told Feb 5. The page shows weekdays but no year; they match 2026 to 2027. Confirm with GHP.
who_can_apply: Skilled and talented high school sophomores and juniors. A Georgia public school district, independent school or state charter school must nominate you. Home school students go through their local school district.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply directly. Ask your school counselor or GHP Coordinator to nominate you. Nominees then complete an online application with a parent permission form, a recommendation and a transcript. GHP project manager: (404) 444-7062.
notes: Local nomination dates differ by school district and the page says they run August to early November, so move fast. Standardized test results are no longer required. The application page is marked updated 08/2026.

name: Georgia Senate Page Program
org: Georgia State Senate (Office of the Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of the Senate)
pay_detail: $20.00 honorarium paid at the end of the day, plus a certificate of service (2025 welcome packet).
duration: One legislative day. Report about 1.5 hours before the Senate convenes. The Senate usually convenes at 10:00 AM (check the Senate schedule the night before).
deadline_text: No application deadline found. Pages choose a legislative day while the General Assembly is in session. The packet says the first 20 days of session fall in January and February. 2027 dates not read.
who_can_apply: Students at least 12 years old. The packet says there are no exceptions. A page is sponsored by the Lieutenant Governor or one Senator.
how_to_apply: The 2025 welcome packet says to contact your sponsoring Senator's office when you register. Staff contact: kim.campbell@senate.ga.gov or illana.burkhart@senate.ga.gov, 404-657-7004. The program web page needs a browser to load, so check it for the current form.
notes: Source is the official 2025 Senate Page welcome packet (the program web pages on legis.ga.gov only showed a loading screen to the reader). Under Georgia law cited in the packet (O.C.G.A. 20-2-692) page service counts as present at school. Dress code is business or business casual. Cell phones are not allowed while paging. The Georgia House has its own page program at legis.ga.gov/house/page-program, which could not be read.

name: STEP: Science, Technology and Engineering Program (Georgia Tech Aerospace Engineering)
org: Georgia Tech Daniel Guggenheim School of Aerospace Engineering
pay_detail: Free to students (funded by industry donors). No stipend stated. Students provide their own daily transportation.
duration: 2-week day program (not residential); Atlanta session July 6 to 17 in 2026
deadline_text: 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are at least 16 years old by the program start. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEP page before the deadline. Questions: outreach@ae.gatech.edu.
notes: Read on the Georgia Space Grant Consortium page that hosts the STEP information; the Georgia Tech Aerospace page itself returned a 403 block. Other sessions listed for 2026 were in Augusta and Albany.

name: Summer Engineering Institute (Georgia Tech College of Engineering)
pay_detail: Free to participants in 2026 (page wording). Participants stay on campus.
duration: 2026 session was June 7 to 15, 2026, overnight on campus
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026 session is closed. No application deadline is shown. Next session dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are rising 11th and 12th graders. You should like engineering, science, math or technology. The page does not mention a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: The page says sign-up is closed for 2026. It does not give application steps. Check the Georgia Tech College of Engineering K-20 initiatives page for the next session.
notes: The same page also describes a separate TryEngineering Summer Institute, a nine day residential program for thirty Georgia high school students at no cost, with no dates given. Georgia residents only.

name: Georgia Work-Based Learning (including Youth Apprenticeship)
org: Georgia Department of Education, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
deadline_text: Set by each school or district. No state dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).

name: WorkSource Georgia Youth (WIOA)
org: Technical College System of Georgia, Office of Workforce Development (WorkSource Georgia)
pay_detail: Free to join. The services page lists paid and unpaid work experiences, but the pages read give no pay rate.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates listed on the state pages.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who face barriers to education, training or employment. Both in-school and out-of-school youth are served. The page does not list the exact barriers or income rules.
how_to_apply: The state pages give no application steps. They give no list of local offices. Use the contact page at tcsg.edu or the WorkSource Georgia portal (worksourcegaportal.com). Find your local office there.
notes: The pages read do not say how to enroll. A call to your local WorkSource office is the real next step. The services page says the Occupational Skills part is for ages 18 to 24. So 14 to 17 year olds would use the other services. Atlanta area teens may also see the city and county programs listed separately in this guide.

name: Teen Gallery Guides @ Getty
org: J. Paul Getty Museum (Getty Center and Getty Villa)
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
deadline_text: The page says the application window typically opens in early February each year. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Girls Inc. of Alameda County High School Programs
city: Oakland, CA (and Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)
deadline_text: Not posted. Contact Girls Inc.
who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: Code the Game is a six week program (the page mentions a fall offering). Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.

name: Girls Who Code Clubs and Pathways
grades: Clubs: grades 3 to 12 (split 3 to 5 and 6 to 12). Pathways: high school.
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.

name: Glenmont Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Aspiring Scientists Summer Internship Program (ASSIP)
org: George Mason University, College of Science
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.
duration: 8 weeks, full time (Jun 18 to Aug 12 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 ASSIP Application is now closed. The page posts no date for the 2027 cycle.
who_can_apply: High school and undergraduate students. Minimum age 15 by Jun 18, 2026 for remote or computer-lab internships and 16 for in-person wet-lab internships. No minimum GPA; transcripts are not requested.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement; interested mentors interview strong candidates and offers go out in early April. Request a fee waiver code from cosassip@gmu.edu if needed.
notes: Labs are at the Fairfax campus, the Science and Technology Campus in Manassas, or Woodbridge; students arrange their own transportation and campus housing cannot be arranged for minors. This is a paid-by-the-student internship, not a job, so no work permit.

name: George Mason University High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: An application fee and college course costs apply. The amounts are not stated on the page read.
duration: One semester at a time, up to 11 lower-level credits
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the page read. Admission is offered for one semester at a time.
who_can_apply: Exceptionally talented high school juniors and seniors. You need a non-degree application and fee. You need your official high school transcript. You need permission from your high school counselor or administrator. Non-native English speakers must meet the English proficiency rule.
how_to_apply: Complete the Non-Degree application. Send your high school transcript. Send your counselor or administrator's permission. Fairfax County Public Schools and Loudoun County Public Schools students can use the school partnership pages. These are for math and science dual enrollment.
notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.

name: Grizzly Youth Academy (National Guard Youth ChalleNGe)
org: California National Guard / California Military Department
city: San Luis Obispo, CA (residential; serves listed central and southern counties)
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).
duration: Residential phase followed by a long check-in phase. The site's pages disagree on the total length (17.5 months on one page, 5.5 months residential plus 24 months after on another), so ask the academy.
deadline_text: No class start dates or deadlines on the pages read. Start with the online Interest Form and a required virtual orientation.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.

name: High School Summer Internship (Georgia Tech Research Institute)
city: Atlanta, GA; Cobb County; Warner Robins, GA (in person)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not on the page.
duration: Five weeks, about June 14 to July 23, 2027; up to 24 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: Pre-application launch is planned for December 11, 2026. The closing date is not listed on the page. The page says dates are approximate and final dates will be in the pre-application.
who_can_apply: Georgia residents in a public, private, charter or home school in Georgia, in the class of 2027, 2028 or 2029, who are 16 by April 4, 2027 (no exceptions). Proof of U.S. citizenship or U.S. person status is required for most positions. You need your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online pre-application. It has a resume (PDF), a personal statement and a letter of recommendation. It must be 100% complete before it closes. You can join the 2027 contact registry for updates. Email support.hsi.stem@gtri.gatech.edu with questions.
notes: No weekend, after hours or remote work. Housing is not provided. Do not send unsolicited emails or calls to GTRI employees about internships. The page asks this. Finishing the pre-application does not guarantee a job. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This internship requires age 16 by April 4, 2027.

name: Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Council (Gwinnett County Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: 40 hours over 6 to 12 months, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
deadline_text: Apply any time. Applications stay on file for six months.
who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. The page says the minimum age is 13 with parental permission required. Homework help covers students in grades K to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form from the Apply Online button on the volunteer page. List the branches you want. If you are a GCPS student, use a personal or parent email, not a school email.
notes: The background check on the page applies only to volunteers 18 and older. Open spots vary by branch.

name: Habitat for Humanity East Bay / Silicon Valley: Volunteer
org: Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page
deadline_text: Ongoing. No sign-up deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.

name: Habitat for Humanity Greater Sacramento: Individual Volunteers (Construction and ReStore)
org: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Sacramento
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)
deadline_text: Rolling. Sign up for shifts after orientation.
who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.

name: Hack Club
pay_detail: Free
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: Join anytime.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.

name: Hacktoberfest 2026
pay_detail: Free
duration: All of October 2026
deadline_text: Runs through October 2026; sign in with MyMLH.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.

name: HandsOn Bay Area Youth Volunteering (HandsOn Tomorrow paused)
grades: High school (for HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Council)

duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks

who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), is paused and is not running in summer 2026. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.

name: ZooTeen Program at Happy Hollow Park and Zoo
org: Happy Hollow Park and Zoo (City of San Jose)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
deadline_text: Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed seasonally. The last orientation listed on the page was Oct 18, 2025 (old); no 2026-27 date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.

name: H.A.R.D. Volunteer Program (Hayward Area Recreation and Park District)
org: Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.)
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.
deadline_text: Opportunities are posted throughout the year. No closing date is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).

name: Hayward Public Library Teen Volunteer Opportunities
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.
deadline_text: Applications are accepted during the school year. No closing date is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.

name: Hayward Youth Commission
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall on the second Monday of each month, September to June, except holidays. The 2021 notice said two-year terms.
deadline_text: 2025 cycle: applications due Friday, May 9, 2025. Interviews were on Friday, May 30, 2025. No 2026 cycle was found.
who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.

name: STEAM Squad teen internship

duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
deadline_text: Hiring dates are not stated. Sign up for Hennepin County job notifications to be told about openings.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the program page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Hiring dates and pay are not on the page. Confirm with the library before relying on it.

name: Teen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated

name: Los Rios Dual Enrollment and CCAP (American River, Cosumnes River, Folsom Lake, Sacramento City)

notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.

name: Madison Children's Museum Volunteers

notes: Volunteer Coordinator: Tim Gruber, tgruber@madisonchildrensmuseum.org. Spots may be limited at any given time, so email before you apply.

name: Accelerated Learning Program (Badger Precollege)

notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited and first come, first served. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.

name: Engineering Summer Program (ESP)

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Massachusetts Wing

name: Maryland Boys State

name: Maryland General Assembly Student Page Program

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library

duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: No fixed deadline on the Join page. Membership lasts Oct. 1 to Sept. 30 and you re-enroll each year.
who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota American Legion Boys State
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted. Each sponsor sets its own. Ask your school counselor or a local American Legion Post.
who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.

name: Minnesota DECA (high school)
org: Minnesota DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines are set by the state advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 28 to Mar 2, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency Minneapolis.
who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.

name: Minnesota FFA
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.
who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.

name: Minnesota House High School Page Program
org: Minnesota House of Representatives, Sergeant at Arms Office
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
deadline_text: Complete applications are due by end of business on Nov 10, 2026 for the 2027 session. Selected students are told by email by mid-December.
who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. You can go to a public or private school or be home schooled. Selection is competitive. The program tries to include students from all parts of the state.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Minnesota Wing
city: Statewide, MN (squadrons in Duluth, St. Paul, Alexandria and more)
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron meeting first.
who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota Youth Council
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
deadline_text: The 2026 round (for the 2026 to 2028 term) took applications from January to March 2026: Feb 28 for priority consideration, Mar 31 for all applications. No 2027 dates are posted. Seats also open when members graduate or step down.
who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.

name: ZooTeen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
deadline_text: Applications for the Summer 2026 ZooTeen camp season are closed. The page says to check the website in 2027 for next summer.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. Follow the term dates.
who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

name: Montgomery County Recreation seasonal part-time jobs
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer camp positions fill in spring.
who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page I read does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Search and Apply' link on the Recreation employment page to apply for seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Summer RISE
org: Montgomery County Public Schools, Department of Partnerships
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Student registration opens in January and runs January to February (year not stated on the page). Placements are announced in April or May.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

name: TeenWorks Employment Program
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
deadline_text: Application windows on the page: Jan 2 to Mar 30 (spring/summer) and Aug 1 to Nov 30 (fall/winter). The page does not state the year, so the fall/winter window may be open now.
who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the program page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Montgomery Parks volunteering and Student Service Learning hours
city: Montgomery County, MD (park sites countywide; office in Wheaton)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Browse the opportunities list and sign up for events.
who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.
how_to_apply: Open the SSL Opportunities list on the Montgomery Parks site. Pick an event approved for SSL hours. Then register. You log in or create a volunteer account. Email parksvolunteers@montgomeryparks.org with questions.
notes: If you need many SSL hours in a short time, the page says that is only sometimes possible. Contacts on the page: Montgomery Parks Customer Service (301) 495-2595, and Volunteer Services 301-495-2504 on the main volunteer page. Office: 2425 Reedie Drive, 12th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 Teen Summer Volunteer Program open in late winter or early spring 2027. No closing date posted yet.
who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

name: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated
duration: School year, August to June
deadline_text: Page still shows an 'Apply now for 2026-2027' banner but gives no closing date; applications opened Feb 6, 2026. Recruitment for the next school year opens each February.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the city YAC page. Questions: yac@mountainview.gov or 650-903-6331.
notes: Meets twice a month, August to June, at 4:30 p.m. in person at The View Teen Center, 263 Escuela Ave. Email to ask whether 2026-27 seats are still open.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)
org: Metropolitan Transportation Commission (with ABAG, BCDC and the Bay Area Air District)
city: Bay Area (virtual sessions, final session in San Francisco)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after completion; amount not stated
duration: 2026: virtual Thursday evening sessions in July plus a final in-person session at Bay Area Metro Center, San Francisco (July 31, 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 program is over. The 2026 call was announced March 24, 2026; exact open and close dates are not on the page. 2027 not posted.
